## What it is

**What it is:** Vaultwarden is a password manager server. It implements the Bitwarden client API in Rust, so the official Bitwarden apps (browser extension, phone, desktop, CLI) can sync a household's passwords, notes and files to a server the owner runs, instead of to a cloud service. It also serves a web vault. It is a much lighter alternative to the official Bitwarden server ([README](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/blob/1.37.5/README.md)). It is one of the contract §8 wave-2 seed apps.

**Licence:** `AGPL-3.0` ([LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/blob/6ed6921cc2b0e03b4d74189574d2a5e71c512e97/LICENSE.txt)). Market class **L2** (copyleft): `research-output/evidence/license-matrix.csv` row "Vaultwarden (Market seed, passwords)" [C-LIC-062]. OneMind ships it unmodified as a separate program, and copies none of its code into the Apache-2.0 core.

**Icon:** A neutral generated icon with initials. Vaultwarden is not associated with Bitwarden, Inc., and the Bitwarden trademarks are separate (README "Disclaimer"), so it is listed only as Vaultwarden and no upstream or Bitwarden logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`, 1 replica) and a `ClusterIP` Service `vaultwarden` on port **8080**, which serves the web vault and the client API.
- State lives on the 1 GiB PVC `vaultwarden-data` at `/data` (the image's `DATA_FOLDER`): the SQLite database `db.sqlite3`, the `rsa_key*` files that sign logins, attachments, sends, the icon cache and `config.json`. Back up the whole volume: the wiki's [Backing up your vault](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/wiki/Backing-up-your-vault) lists what each file is for.
- It runs as UID/GID 65534 (`nobody`), not root, with no privilege escalation, all Linux capabilities dropped and the default seccomp profile. The image runs as root by default. The wiki page [Running docker container with non-root user](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/wiki/Running-docker-container-with-non-root-user) documents this setup, with `ROCKET_PORT` at 1024 or higher, so it listens on 8080.
- Probes: readiness and liveness `GET /alive`, the endpoint the image's own `HEALTHCHECK` calls (`docker/healthcheck.sh`).
- **Admin page off:** no `ADMIN_TOKEN` is set, so `/admin` is disabled, as the wiki describes in [Enabling admin page](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/wiki/Enabling-admin-page) under "Disabling the admin page".

**Sizing:** Upstream publishes no resource figures. The requests (50m CPU, 64 MiB) and limits (500m CPU, 256 MiB) are a OneMind choice: in the smoke test on k3s (arm64) the idle server used 1m CPU and 6 MiB of memory, so the limits leave room for syncs, icon downloads and attachments. The Market lists `minMemoryMb: 256`.

## First run

Source: the upstream [README](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/blob/1.37.5/README.md) "Usage" section, and the wiki pages [Enabling HTTPS](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/wiki/Enabling-HTTPS) and [Disable registration of new users](https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden/wiki/Disable-registration-of-new-users).

1. Install Vaultwarden from the Market and approve the action. It installs into the namespace `app-vaultwarden`.
2. The web vault needs HTTPS or `localhost`, because it uses the browser's Web Crypto API, which only works in a secure context. For a first test, forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-vaultwarden port-forward svc/vaultwarden 8080:8080
   ```
   For phones and other devices, put it behind HTTPS (the wiki recommends a reverse proxy) and set `DOMAIN` to that URL.
3. Select "Create account" and create the owner's account. Upstream's default lets **anyone who can reach the server** register (`SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=true`).
4. When every household member has an account, turn registration off. Add `SIGNUPS_ALLOWED` with value `"false"` to the container's `env` in `manifests/deployment.yaml`, then reinstall. Organization owners can still invite people afterwards.
5. In the Bitwarden apps, choose "self-hosted" and enter the server URL.

## Not done yet

- No HTTPS or `DOMAIN`: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web vault works only through `localhost` until a reverse proxy exists.
- No SMTP: email verification, invitations by email and password hints by email are off.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set: it has not been tested against this image.
- `spec.updates.automerge` is `none`: patch automerge needs this app added to the automerge list in `renovate.json` (validate-apps check 9), a separate change outside this app directory.
